children: The Indian rupee extended the gains as it opened strong against the US dollar on October 13, after the Reserve Bank of India announced more measures to alleviate pressure on the currency.
The rupee opened higher by 62 paise at 95.16 per dollar, compared with Monday’s close of 95.78.

According to Finrex, after RBIs steps to keep a tab on the rupee fall, markets were wary of buying dollars as rupee closed at its one-month high giving small importers a relief to buy their payables while bigger importers had to pay extra in the form of FERR to banks for hedging their positions.

Rupee set to open around 95.51 this morning as RBI ensures momentarily rupee does not fall beyond 96 levels moving within a range of 95 to 96 for the day with exporters to sell the upticks (for cash) and importers to continue buying the dips hedging their imports payable in October and November, it added.

Asian currencies traded lower against the US dollar, with the South Korean won leading the losses, declining 0.214 percent, followed by the Taiwan dollar, which fell 0.175 percent. The Philippine peso and Indonesian rupiah also depreciated by 0.129 percent and 0.078 percent, respectively. The Thai baht, Chinese renminbi and Malaysian ringgit edged lower by 0.027 percent, 0.016 percent and 0.015 percent, respectively. Meanwhile, the Japanese yen appreciated 0.152 percent and the Singapore dollar remained unchanged.

The dollar held its ground at the start of Asian trading on Tuesday after a holiday for some markets in the US, as geopolitical risks rose after renewed attacks on energy infrastructure in the Middle East and Ukraine.

The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 102.56 in subdued Asian trading after closing up 0.3% on Monday. The currency is hovering around its highest levels since April last year.

title: Currency Check: Rupee extends gain, opens 62 paise higher at 95.16 per dollar
